interest: It documents SCAP's balance between commercial reopening and security screening. It also reveals postwar refugee movements through occupied Japan.
overview: This file documents the regulation and administrative control of travel, residence, and foreign commercial activity in occupied Japan from July 1948 through April 1949, coordinated among the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, and the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). It features key occupation directives—notably SCAP Circulars Nos. 1, 2, 19, and 21, and SCAPIN 1966—which governed private commercial entrants, foreign investment, and customs and currency controls. The bulk of the correspondence, applications, and military permits concerns international merchants seeking to re-establish trade in textiles, pearls, and industrial supplies, alongside records of missionary travel, the establishment of sixty-day family visits with Japanese relatives, humanitarian repatriations, and the transit of displaced persons fleeing China.
